News.title: ‘We very much need girls’: Putin’s spies on the hunt for young female agents to bolster Russia’s espionage ranks
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin is on the hunt for young female spies as the desperate dictator seeks to recruit new agents.

Recruitment drives are underway at Russian universities looking for new agents like the notorious Anna Chapman.





At prestigious Novosibirsk State University in Siberia, students were summoned to a compulsory meeting.

They were told by spy bosses: “Even if you’ve tried cannabis three or four times, you still have a chance of joining us.”

The SVR – Russia’s foreign intelligence service – is looking for “people who know how to obtain up-to-date information according to the goals and tasks set, process it, analyse it properly, and report it”.



At ex-KGB agent Putin’s former St Petersburg State University, spy Tamara Netyksa told students: “We very much need intelligent, serious, good, well-prepared boys and girls.

“We very much need girls”, she stressed.

Veteran Russian intelligence officer Elena Vavilova, 63, told students: “The highest level in intelligence work is when a source begins to tell you themselves about their work, to confide in you.”

Vavilova posed in Canada and the US as Tracey Ann Foley, and was married to another illegal agent Andrey Bezrukov, known as Donald Howard Heathfield.



Their cover was blown in 2010 when Russian glamour spy Anna Chapman, then a British citizen after a marriage to a Briton, was detained by the FBI.

Flame-haired Chapman said she was recruited by Mad Vlad’s SVR after a London-based Russian agent became intrigued with her networking skills, in particular her hold over wealthy and influential men.

She wove her way into the British business and political elite deploying what she called “the necessary attributes”.

Chapman admitted: “I knew the effect I had on men.

“Nature had generously endowed me with the necessary attributes: a slim waist, a full chest, and a cascade of red hair.



“All I needed was to emphasise it – which I did with simple yet sexy outfits, light makeup, and an effortless air about me. I never wore jewellery – I didn’t feel the need for it.”

Chapman had become a British citizen after marrying Brit Alex Chapman, now dead.

She wrote a book about her time in London which included trips to Paris and Geneva with mega-wealthy lovers and admirers – and a strip-poker session with a group of multi-millionaires.

Chapman bragged: “Most importantly, I didn’t try too hard to please.



“People can always sense when someone is desperate for approval, and it has the opposite effect.

“That’s what happens with overly dressed-up girls or overly chatty men. I never sought anyone’s approval – I simply was myself.

“And it worked like magic.”

It comes after The Sun revealed that a former KGB spy who was trained to seduce high-profile targets was now warning how female agents use the same playbook to steal secrets from the West.



Aliia Roza, 41, was taught the art of seduction, influence and manipulation by authorities to target drug gangs and people traffickers on their behalf.

The daughter of a high-ranking officer and the granddaughter of a Second World War “national hero”, was just 18 years old when she was shipped off to a KGB military academy for the sons and daughters of the top officials .

She undertook the same programme Putin graduated from in 1975.

Taught charm, psychology and emotional connection, Aliia learnt to extract information from her targets, who were often powerful men.

“When we were enrolled, we were told not to share these techniques with anyone – not even our colleagues or friends,” she said.



“Lots of it is about psychological techniques, the psychology of men – for example, what are their weaknesses? What are their needs? What are they scared of? What do they desire?

“When you learn the psychology of different personalities, you understand how to manipulate, how to make them do what you want.”

After graduating, she joined the FSB – the KGB’s modern successor that Putin was formerly in charge of – where she was tasked with infiltrating drug and human trafficking gangs.

Aliia revealed agents followed the same playbook to break down their target’s defences – without them suspecting a thing.



The spy-turned-influencer insisted these very tactics were being used by Russian and Chinese spies to prey on targets in Western countries – including the UK and US.

Just last year, two Bulgarian women were linked to a Russian spy ring in the UK, where they allegedly worked in the elaborate and life-threatening “honey-trap” surveillance operation, according to the BBC.

The spy ring, who carried out espionage operations for Vladimir Putin’s regime in Britain while bedding each other, were caught in March 2025.

Cvetelina Gencheva and Tsvetanka Doncheva were both accused of being linked to the London cell which saw two other women jailed.



Glamorous lab assistant Katrin Ivanova, 33, and beautician Vanya Gaberova, 30, were convicted at the Old Bailey of espionage offences under the Official Secrets Act.

Gaberova’s painter and decorator ex-boyfriend Tihomir Ivanchev, 39, of Enfield, North London, was also convicted of spying charges.

In court, two other mystery women who took part in surveillance operations across Europe had been mentioned – believed to be Gencheva and Doncheva.

The women were all linked back to Russian spymaster Orlin Roussev, after he commissioned Ivanova and Gaberova to steal reporter Christo Grozev’s laptop, after he unmasked the Salisbury Novichok poisoners.

The duo travelled to a conference in Spain, accompanied by Bizer Dzhambazov, 43, who was living with Ivanova but having an affair with Gaberova.



On September 12, 2021, Roussev reported to Marsalek on the encrypted Telegram app the operation to follow Grozev from Vienna to Valencia “with the couple and the ground team” had “worked flawlessly“.

Joking about the Novichok poisoning of Navalny, he added: “Feels like we must poison him next just to live up to past stories. Ideally using his underwear or his cap.”

Roussev later added: “I have twins on the surveillance team.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“One of the killer sexy brunettes will enter the conference.”

Roussev and Dzhambazov later admitted conspiracy to collect information useful to an enemy.

News.title: Schools will be forced to ban phones by law
News.content:
The climbdown comes as ministers battle to push their children’s reforms through Parliament before time runs out

RUNG OUT Schools will be forced to ban phones by law

SCHOOLS will be forced to ban mobile phones by law after a late scramble by ministers to get their plans through the Lords.

The Government is rushing through an amendment to give phone bans legal backing after pressure from peers threatened to stall the legislation.



Until now, schools were only advised to go phone-free, with no legal requirement to enforce it.



A Department for Education spokesman said mobiles have “no place in schools” and the change will “give legal force to what schools are already doing”.

They added: “It builds on the steps we’ve already taken to strengthen enforcement, with Ofsted considering schools’ mobile phone policies as part of inspection from this month.

“We will always put children’s interests first, including through this Bill – which is widely recognised as the biggest piece of child safeguarding legislation in decades, with critical measures like laws to crack down on profiteering in children’s social care and a new unique identifier to stop children falling through the cracks.”

The move comes ahead of a crunch vote in the House of Lords, with Tory peers pushing hard on the issue.

The climbdown comes as ministers battle to push their children’s reforms through Parliament before time runs out.

Shadow Education Secretary Laura Trott said: “I am delighted we have forced Labour to see sense and U-turn. This is fantastic news for headteachers, parents and pupils across the country.

“For over a year, Labour dismissed this as an unnecessary gimmick, and just last week the Education Minister claimed the problem had already been solved.

“I’m glad they’ve now listened, this is the right step for improving behaviour and raising attainment in our classrooms.”

News.title: D4vd ‘murdered Celeste Rivas Hernandez to protect career as he feared sick sex crimes with 14-year-old would be exposed’
News.content:
SINGER D4vd has been charged with first-degree murder – seven months after the grim discovery of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s dismembered body in his abandoned Tesla.

The charges were announced during a press conference at 10am on Monday in Los Angeles after D4vd was arrested last week.





LAPD Chief Jim McDonnell addressed the media and Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman laid out their case.

Hochman said he was announcing the charges against the singer, real name David Anthony Burke, after the “brutal and horrific murder,” which he described as a “parent’s worst nightmare”.

He said they are bringing the most serious charges that a DA’s office can bring: first degree murder with special circumstances and he is facing life without the possibility of parole.

There are three sets of charges, and the special circumstances include “lying in wait,” and that the murder was committed for “financial gain”.

He is accused of murdering a witness to an investigation to maintain his lucrative music career that Celeste was “threatening” on the night she went to his house and never returned home.

Hochman said he is accused of “lewd and lascivious acts” with a minor.

He said the full details of the special circumstances will be discussed in court in the coming weeks and it had been a “very rigorous and thorough investigation.”



Hochman also appealed to anyone who has information related to Celeste’s murder to come forward and said there is “forensic and digital evidence” for the case.

“The coroner’s report will be released shortly,” he added, explaining the coroner has made a determination as to how Celeste was killed.

McDonnell also addressed Celeste’s family and said that today was a “step towards healing” and they are committed to seeking justice.

They announced Beth Silverman will be the lead prosecutor on the case.

The news comes after the teen’s remains were found in September 2025.



Celeste’s family are also set to speak through their attorney, Patrick Steinfeld, after the charges were announced.

The teen’s father, Jesus Rivas, previously spoke through their lawyer after D4vd’s arrest, saying, “Thank God…justice for Celeste.”

He added that the family was “committed to ensuring that Celeste’s voice is heard.”

D4vd, 21, was arrested on suspicion of murder on Thursday after armed officers smashed down the door of his Hollywood Hills rental.

The singer was seen being led away in handcuffs in photographs published by the California Post before being held without bail over the weekend.



The case was then presented to the Major Crimes Division and prosecutors reviewed the facts to determine whether they met the threshold to file charges.

A grand jury was previously convened and spent months trying to gather evidence and lock in testimony amid mounting criticism.

A Tesla registered to the Houston-born artist was found abandoned at a Hollywood tow yard last year.

Police searched the car after workers complained of a foul smell coming from inside.

They found Celeste’s decomposed remains on September 8 and she is believed to have been dead for weeks, officials said.



Investigators recovered a cadaver bag containing a head and torso and a second bag with various other body parts inside, officials later confirmed.

Celeste had been missing since April 2024 – when she was just 13 years old – and is said to have repeatedly run away from home while dating D4vd, according to family and friends.

The Medical Examiner has ruled the teen’s death a homicide.

Timeline in the death of Celeste Rivas Hernandez April 2024 – Celeste Rivas Hernandez, 13, is reported missing from Lake Elsinore, California. August 5, 2025 – D4vd starts his Withered World Tour. August 27: A traffic officer marks D4vd’s Tesla over an issue relating to its tires. September 3: D4vd’s Tesla given a citation. September 5– D4vd’s Tesla is towed to a Hollywood yard. September 7 – Rivas turns 15 years old. September 8 – The Los Angeles Police Department discovered a dismembered body wrapped in plastic in the trunk of D4vd’s impounded Tesla. September 17 – The decomposing body is identified as Celeste Rivas. September 18 – D4vd’s house is searched overnight and investigators take a computer and other evidence. D4vd continues his tour with a show in Seattle. Rivas’s family breaks their silence on their GoFundMe page. September 19 – D4vd cancels the rest of his tour. September 23 – Rivas’s body is released to her family. It’s revealed that D4vd and his manager have broken their lease and left the house that was raided in Hollywood. October 6 – Rivas is buried in a private funeral ceremony in Rowland Heights, California. April 16 – D4vd arrested on suspicion of murder and his lawyers vow to defend him. April 20 – Charges are announced at a press conference in Los Angeles as Celeste’s family speaks out.

D4vd’s attorneys, Blair Berk, Marilyn Bednarski, and Regina Peter, vowed to “vigorously defend” his client’s innocence.

“Let us be clear — the actual evidence in this case will show that David Burke did not murder Celeste Rivas Hernandez and he was not the cause of her death,” they said.



Experts told The U.S. Sun they believe the arrest took so long as investigators tried to get D4vd’s inner circle to tell the truth about what they knew.

RJ Dreiling, a former Los Angeles County deputy district attorney, said, “When we have a body decomposing in a car with no clear suspects at the beginning, it can take a long time for investigators to piece things together with forensic evidence and interviews.

“It’s not like a typical murder case where there’s a shooting or a stabbing, where the police arrive and arrest someone.”

He added, “Bail for a murder is $2 million. If prosecutors ask for no bail, they will need to present evidence that he is a flight risk or that he could cause harm to the public.”

Dreiling, who is not connected to the case, also warned that it is complex and prosecutors have a challenge on their hands.



He said, “They will have to tie D4vd to the crime. The main issue they have above everything else is proving it was a homicide, not accidental death, and they must prove D4vd is the one who did it.

“I expect the defense will say D4vd wasn’t involved and argue there isn’t even enough proof this was a murder.

“And those could be very winning arguments, especially if the forensic evidence and the witness statements don’t line up.”

The rising star, who had previously played Coachella Festival, was on his Withered World Tour when the discovery was made.

He suddenly pulled the plug on his remaining concerts and hadn’t been seen in public prior to his arrest.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

D4vd first found fame with songs like Romantic Homicide and Here With Me, which have amassed billions of streams.

He gained a following by livestreaming himself playing video games, and then started releasing music that went viral on TikTok.

News.title: Trump warns it’s ‘highly unlikely’ US-Iran ceasefire will be extended after deadline – & Strait blockade is set to last
News.content:
DONALD Trump has warned it is “highly unlikely” that the two-week ceasefire with Iran will be extended past the Wednesday deadline.

Iran has been accused of stalling peace talks with huge disagreements continuing to dog progress between both sides as the shaky ceasefire between the enemies teeters on the brink of collapse.





A second round of talks are due to resume later today in the Pakistani capital, Islamabad.

But Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei has declared the regime has “no plan for the next round of negotiations” amid fears the US delegation would be stood up.

It remains unclear if the talks will go ahead.



The current shaky truce between the America and the rogue state is due to expire at around 1am UK time on Wednesday as tensions between the US and Iran continue to mount with no sign of compromise.

Trump said earlier today: “I’m not going to be rushed into making a bad deal. We’ve got all the time in the world.”

When asked about the ceasefire, Trump told Bloomberg: “It is Wednesday evening. Wednesday evening Washington time.”

He further reiterated his intentions about the future of the regime, taking to Truth Social to say Iran must accept peace terms.



The main sticking points between the two sides remain Tehran’s enriched uranium, its missile programme and allowing safe passage through the paralysed Strait of Hormuz oil route.

Baghaei has already flatly rejected all three US demands.

Trump – who has vowed to blitz every power station and bridge in Iran if no deal is reached – vented his frustration at the mullahs’ apparent no-show at peace talks.

He said: “They’re supposed to be there. We agreed to be there, although they say we didn’t.

“It was set up. And we’ll see whether or not it’s there. If they’re not there, that’s fine too.”



Trump went on to say that the regime should be appreciative of his offer.

He added: “The results in Iran will be amazing – And if Iran’s new leaders (Regime Change!) are smart, Iran can have a great and prosperous future!”

He also insisted that he won’t reopen the Strait of Hormuz to the dismay of the Iranian government after the US launched a blockade over the weekend.

“They want me to open it. The Iranians desperately want it opened. I’m not opening it until a deal is signed,” Trump said.

Tensions spiralled overnight after a US warship blasted and seized an Iranian ship attempting to dodge the American blockade.



American military chiefs released video of the USS Spruance warship blasting the engine room of the Iranian cargo vessel Touska on Sunday.

Dramatic audio showed a US Navy captain ordering the Iranian crew “vacate your engine room” before a volley of shells disabled the ship’s power plant.



US marines then slid down ropes onto the ship from helicopters launched by the USS Tripoli assault ship to take control of the vessel.

The ship’s captain was said to have “failed to comply with repeated warnings” from US forces over a six-hour period before the first ship seizure was ordered.

Trump said: “Our Navy ship stopped them right in their tracks by blowing a hole in the engine room.”

Iran’s Khatam al-Anbiya military HQ vowed that Iran would avenge the “violation of the ceasefire” and launched drones toward US ships, though no damage was reported.

Its statement read: “Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran will soon respond to and retaliate for this act of armed piracy by the US Navy.”



Peace hopes slumped further as a former commander in Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps declared it his nation’s “inalienable right” to control the Strait of Hormuz oil route.

Ebrahim Azizi said: “Iran will decide the right of passage, including permissions for vessels to pass through the Strait.”

Iranian military chiefs pledged further revenge as Brent crude oil prices jumped five per cent to $94-a-barrel as the reignited conflict continues to rock global markets.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Iran conflict has already triggered the largest global energy supply disruption in history following the closure of the Hormuz channel which carries a fifth of the world’s oil and gas.

Market pressure has led to record fuel prices, high inflation and a growing risk of global recession – amid fear of further spikes if the war escalates.

News.title: Major motorway closes after multi-car crash & fire leaves drivers stuck for 30 minutes in 3 miles of traffic
News.content:
SMASH CHAOS Major motorway closes after multi-car crash & fire leaves drivers stuck for 30 minutes in 3 miles of traffic

A MAJOR UK motorway has been fully closed following a multiple vehicle collision.

Drivers have been told to expect 30 minute delays with three miles of congestion.



The eastbound carriageway of the M62 in West Yorkshire has been entirely shut down between J29 and J30.



Emergency services were rushed to the scene following reports of a serious collision involving multiple vehicles.

The crash happened between junction 29 for the M1 at Lofthouse and junction 30 at Rothwell at around 4:15pm on April 20.

The westbound side of the carriageway also has three of its four lanes closed.

National Highways has warned drivers of 30 minute delays with congestion reaching three miles long.

Another incident has also happened on the A303 between the A30 in Micheldever and the A34 in Lower Bullington today.

The motorway has remained closed eastbound following a police led incident.

With Hampshire Police at the scene, drivers are experiencing 10 minutes of delays and one mile of congestion on the south England highway.

News.title: Thousands of migrants line up for citizenship documents after socialist Spain opens its doors to up to 1.3MILLION
News.content:
RUBBER STAMP-EDE Thousands of migrants line up for citizenship documents after socialist Spain opens its doors to up to 1.3MILLION

HUGE queues have formed in cities across Spain as the socialist-led country approved plans to give legal status to hundreds of thousands of migrants.

Migrants waited for hours in enormous lines, with some even staying overnight, desperate to get their paperwork rubber-stamped.





The scheme gives legal status to all foreign nationals who can prove they do not have a criminal record, entered Spain before the start of 2026 and have lived in the country for at least five months at the time they apply.

Online applications opened last Thursday after the programme was approved by PM Pedro Sánchez’s socialist government.

Now hopeful migrants are waiting at more than 400 locations across the country for in-person appointments.

Seville’s town hall considered closing early due to the huge numbers of people waiting, according to Diario de Sevilla.



One Columbian migrant waiting in Barcelona told El Periodico that he had arrived at “around 10 or 11pm last night so we wouldn’t be left out” and had been waiting around 15 hours.

A Honduran migrant told the paper he had slept on the floor to save his place in the queue, adding: “A very large group of people almost trampled me… We risked our lives, but it will be worth it.”

Successful applicants will be allowed to work legally and receive a one-year residency permit, with the option to extend.

The Spanish government first estimated that this would give legal status to around 500,000 people.



But analysis by the National Centre for Immigration and Borders (CNIF) later suggested that between 750,000 and one million illegal migrants currently in Spain would apply for legal status.

And a further 250,000 to 350,000 asylum seekers may also seek legal status.

Experts forecast “secondary movements” of up to 250,000 illegal migrants per year from other Schengen-area countries into Spain over the medium to long term.

It means a total of up to 1.3million people could now be granted legal status through the scheme.

Thousands of migrants descended on their consulates across Spain last week to get documents to prove they do not have a criminal record.



A huge queue formed outside the Pakistani consulate in January, before the plan had been fully confirmed.

Tech mogul Elon Musk then got into a row with left wing Socialist Sánchez over the policy.

Musk’s fracas with the PM started when the X-owner reposted a tweet that claimed PM Sanchez was “dropping the mask” with blatant “electoral engineering” “under the guise of defeating the far-right”.



Musk shared the X post and added “wow”, enraging Sanchez, who hit back.

The Spanish PM replied: “Mars can wait. Humanity can’t.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It was a jab at Musk’s Starship project, which is trying to create the most powerful rocket in the world as part of SpaceX’s bid to take humanity to Mars.

Socialist Sánchez argues that his plan is needed to combat workforce shortages, and boost his country’s ailing economy.

News.title: Moment Reform MP is KICKED OUT of Commons after branding Keir Starmer a liar
News.content:
A REFORM MP was booted out of the Commons today for accusing Sir Keir Starmer of “lying”.

Lee Anderson blasted the PM’s defence of appointing Peter Mandelsonas US Ambassador, warning “no one believes him”.





In a question to Sir Keir, the outspoken politician blasted: “The public doesn’t believe him, the MPs on this side of the House don’t believe him, his own gullible backbenchers don’t believe him, so does the PM agree with me he’s been lying?”

Mr Anderson was told off by Commons Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle.

Under archaic parliamentary rules MPs cannot be accused of lying.



But after being told to withdraw his comment, Mr Anderson responded: “I will not withdraw – that man couldn’t lie straight in bed.”

He was subsequently ordered to leave the chamber.

Zarah Sultana was also removed from the Chamber by Sir Lindsay after she accused the Prime Minister of being a “bare-faced liar”.

In a question, the Your Party MP (Coventry South) said: “We all know that the Prime Minister appointed Mandelson because he owes his job to him. He appointed him, he defended him, and now he claims to know nothing.



“He is gaslighting the nation. So let’s call this out for what it is. The Prime Minister is a bare-faced liar.”

Sir Lindsay said: “Leave now, I’ll name you otherwise, I’d go now if I were you.

“I’ve given the option to name. I’d leave if I were you, very quickly.”

Ms Sultana attempted to interject and said: “I have a duty to the House to tell the truth.”

Sir Lindsay held a vote, brought by Government whip Gen Kitchen which said: “I beg to move that Zarah Sultana be suspended from the services of the House.”



MPs voted in favour.

“Leave, I’m sorry you’ve done this, I really am,” Sir Lindsay said.

It comes as Sir Keir today admitted it was “staggering” he was never told Mandelson had failed top-level security vetting – as he scrambled to contain the deepening row.

The PM insisted officials granted Mandelson clearance despite a formal recommendation it should be denied and did not tell him, the Foreign Secretary or even the Cabinet Secretary.

He also confirmed the Foreign Office’s power to overrule vetting decisions has now been suspended, and a fresh probe into the system launched.



The crisis erupted after The Guardian revealed Mandelson had failed security vetting last week, triggering the sacking of senior official Sir Olly Robbins.

Addressing the Commons today, Sir Keir pointed the finger at Foreign Office officials, accusing them of failing to “sensibly flag” the recommendation before Mandelson took up the Washington role.

The PM said there was “no law” preventing civil servants from warning ministers about vetting concerns while protecting sensitive details.

He told MPs: “The recommendation in the Peter Mandelson case could and should have been shared with me before he took up his post,..

“If I had known before he took up his post, the UKSV (United Kingdom Security Vetting ) recommendation was that developed vetting clearance would be denied, I would not have gone ahead with the appointment.”



The PM said he found it “astonishing” and “staggering” that not only was he kept in the dark — but the then Cabinet Secretary was also not told during a formal review of the appointment.

He went on: “I know many members across the House will find these facts to be incredible, and to that I can only say that they are right. It beggars belief that throughout the whole timeline of events, officials in the Foreign Office saw fit to withhold this information from the most senior ministers in our system of government.

“That is not how the vast majority of people in this country expects politics, government or accountability to work, and I do not think it’s how most public servants think it should work.”

The row comes after Sir Keir insisted three times at PMQs — just a day before Mandelson was sacked — that “full due process” had been followed.

Ministers are expected to correct the record swiftly if they mislead Parliament, even inadvertently.



But the Tories say the PM has failed to do so, despite being told last Tuesday that Mandelson had failed vetting.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch accused the Prime Minister of breaching the ministerial code by waiting nearly a week to come to the Commons.

She said: “His reputation is at stake. Everyone is watching. It is finally time for the truth.”

Arguing that Sir Keir Starmer inadvertently misled the House, she said: “I will remind him that, under the ministerial code, he has a duty to correct the record at the earliest opportunity.

“The Prime Minister says he only found out on Tuesday that Peter Mandelson failed the security vetting. The earliest opportunity to correct the record was Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday, almost a week ago. This is a breach of the ministerial code.”



Responding, Sir Keir said: “When I found out what had happened on Tuesday evening last, I wanted to have answers to the question: who made the decision to recommend to give clearance on developed vetting, contrary to the advice, why that was done and who knew about it, so I could provide the information to the House.

“That is the exercise that’s been conducted since Tuesday evening and today, so that I could come here today to give the full account to the House, which I’ve just set out.”

Fresh documents published hours before today’s Commons statement also show Sir Keir was warned to wait for checks to be completed before confirming the appointment.

Ahead of hiring the Labour peer, then Cabinet Secretary Lord Case told the PM: “You should give us the name of the person you would like to appoint and we will develop a plan for them to acquire the necessary security clearances and do due diligence on any potential Conflicts of Interest or other issues of which you should be aware before confirming your choice.”

It raises questions over why Sir Keir did not wait for the vetting to be done before announcing Lord Mandelson to the public as his man in Washington.



The axed Foreign Office chief will give his own evidence to MPs tomorrow to set out his version of events.

Sir Keir is under huge pressure over a slew of policy U-turns, dismal poll ratings and calls for him to resign — but allies have told wannabe leadership challengers to put the country first.

Senior government sources have claimed it was Mandelson’s foreign links that led to a recommendation against his appointment, rather than his friendship with paedophile financier Jeffrey Epstein.

Mandelson was sacked last year less than 12 months after he was appointed when details emerged of his ties with Epstein.

It was revealed last week that he was not granted developed vetting status during the appointment process but this was overturned by Sir Olly, who did not tell No 10.



However, No 10 believes he had the opportunity to raise the report on four different occasions.

It says it could have been disclosed when he saw the advice or when Mandelson was sacked.

Insiders revealed he could have also raised the issue when the Government was forced to release material on the appointment and also when ministers said they would review security vetting last month.

But he was not stopped by law from “sensibly flagging” recommendations from the vetting body regarding Mandelson’s appointment, a Government document reveals.

Paperwork released last night says there is “nothing in the guidance” that prevented details being shared in the Mandelson scenario.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The law states that civil servants make decisions on vetting and clearance but they can raise recommendations to ministers to make judgments, appointments or even explaining matters to Parliament.

It states that this could have been done in a “proportionate and necessary way” if in line with the appropriate steps.

News.title: I visited US fat capital ‘designed to make you obese’… where 28st locals wear size XXXXXL & scoff 10k calories a DAY
News.content:
TWENTY-EIGHT stone Rudy Mendiola wipes his mouth after his daily, 5,000-calorie junk food meal and tells me: “This is the danger zone.”

Welcome to America’s fat ­capital, where the air is choked with stale oil from endless fast food restaurants and stores are stacked with giant clothes for supersized shoppers.



I’m in McAllen, southern Texas, a town with an outsized reputation as the fattest place in America, a ­dubious honour it has held for the past three years.



Half of the 150,000 population in this calorie-laden outpost is obese, and another third is overweight.

Uber driver Rudy, 48, tells me it’s “normal” to be fat in McAllen, and he is right. Everywhere you look, there are oversized people.

It is little wonder, given it is a place where fizzy drinks are cheaper than water at a dollar each, residents typically munch through 10,000 calories a day, and food is described by locals as a dangerous “drug”.

The town is home to 500 fast food restaurants — that is one per every 300 people.

In one of the popular all-you-can-eat Chinese buffets, people are so addicted they cannot even wait to take a table before tucking in — a warning sign on the wall tells diners to step away from the food counters before delving into their brimming plates.



Within one minute of driving into McAllen, I was confronted with ten giant neon signs displaying $5 (£3.50) pizzas, $6 burger ­combos and $4 tacos.

The city also seems designed to ­fatten people. It is nigh on impossible to walk. There are no pavements alongside 55mph-limit roads, no cycle lanes, only a handful of gyms — and everything is a drive-thru.

Motorised scooters that you can rent via a mobile phone app for the day to save waddling around are in shopping malls and supermarkets.

Rudy, who is looking for love but bemoans that his last date was a catfish as she was “too big”, says: “It’s normal to be overweight here, so ­people don’t lose it as no one judges.”

He adds: “I know I eat more than I’m supposed to, and I eat the wrong foods.



“I don’t get long breaks and have to grab fast food. That’s Whata- burger, Chinese food or chicken strips.

“I can sometimes only eat one meal a day, but it could be in excess of 5,000 calories. Coffees and drinks rack up more calories.

“I’ve had two knee surgeries, as the weight I have on my body means three times as much stress for my knees.

“I have arthritis and chronic kidney stones. It’s a danger zone here.”

Even teenagers in the city recognise that the locals are on the front line of an obesity crisis which is destroying the nation’s health.



And with worrying echoes of the US fentanyl crisis, where whole towns became awash with abuse of the prescription painkiller, Bella Lopez, 18, said: “The food here has become almost a drug.”

It’s cheaper to buy takeout food than make it at home. Luis

At the local Walmart, where they sell XXXXXL clothes, I meet Rose, 31, who weighs more than 25st, and her husband Luis, 26, weighing 26st, who have a starkly worded warning: “You will get fat if you move here.”

They also explain how the heavy influence of Texas’s Mexican immigrant population has supercharged the ­obesity problem.

Luis, who is of Mexican origin, is out shopping with their three children. He says: “There’s a lot of ­Mexican culture here, which is all about food, and that meets Texan culture, where the mantra is everything is bigger.

“The portion sizes become way ­bigger, even in supermarkets.”



Luis holds up a three-litre bottle of Diet Coke — special to the area — as an example.

“It’s cheaper to buy takeout food than make it at home,” he explains.

“Even with the kids, we needed to do the food shopping and the fastest thing to get them was a basket of fries and chicken tenders, which were being sold at the front of the store.”

He admits the family’s favourite snack is Chicharron, a popular dish of fried pork belly or pork rinds, with a Mexican cola, which uses cane sugar instead of corn syrup, but adds: “We have been trying hard to lose weight.



“We gained during Covid because pre-Covid I was 210lbs (15st) and went up to 390lbs (27st 12lbs). Now I’m down to 360lbs (25st 10lbs).

“We are desperate to get healthy.”



The same can’t be said for the lady in front of us, who is buying 24 cans of cola, two bags of pork scratchings, a bag of Oreo cookies, cookie dough biscuits and cheese crackers.

There is not a vegetable in sight.

‘Snacking is a big thing’

Laura Landeros, 61, who has to use a mobility scooter to get around the store due to her weight, proudly tells us: “Snacking is a big thing here. If you don’t have snacks, you’re boring.

“My favourites are these pork cracklings and Doritos. I make a ­guacamole cream sauce for them.

“I’m a hardcore Coca-Cola fan, too, but my favourite is Dr Pepper, the cherry flavour.”



Outside the supermarket, dozens of vending machines offer dollar (70p) fizzy drinks.

And the local petrol ­station, Stripes, sells a 1.5litre cup of pop of your choice, called the Big Gulp, for just a dollar, while a 500ml bottle of water is $3 (£2.20).

As local demand is so high, Coca-Cola operates a massive distribution centre on the edge of town.

Dietitian Brandon Harper, who runs Harper/Cook nutrition with his wife, says residents here can easily ­consume more than 10,000 calories a day and eat all three meals out.

He said: “We have a really big influence from Mexican culture.



“A quesadilla would normally ­consist of two tortillas with a bit of chicken and cheese, but it becomes super-sized.

“It becomes two massive tortillas and mountains of cheese with excess protein and added avocado and tortilla chips. It becomes huge.

“And everyone here lives a ­sedentary life.”

There are bed-bound people here who are over 400lbs. Nurse Daniela Delgardo

The Black Bear diner is home to a 1,710-calorie breakfast named The Volcano — and your insides could erupt with the three sweet cream pancakes, two sausages, two slices of thick-cut bacon and maple syrup.

I tried the meal, and after just three bites, I felt sick to the point I was heaving from the overload of sugar.



It made me feel so ill that I couldn’t eat a thing for the rest of the day. I was bent over double on the side of the restaurant, praying that I would vomit.

Texan fast food franchise Whataburger, with its distinctive orange ‘W’ logo, is a beacon for locals, and its triple cheeseburger combo meal is one of the most popular items.

It comes in at 2,220 calories — more than a woman’s recommended daily limit of 2,000 calories.

One hefty man queuing for his cheeseburger said: “Loads of people here eat fast food for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Why not? It’s tasty and cheap.”

He adds that the town had to open more branches of the burger chain because the queues were so big.



There are now six in a tiny radius.

Nurse Daniela Delgardo, who works on the cardiac unit at the hospital in the region, told The Sun: “We see a lot of high blood pressure and ­diabetes, which is life-threatening.

‘Can’t fit through my door’

“There are bed-bound people here who are over 400lbs (28st 8lbs).

“There’s a lot of access to fast food, which contains sodium and artificial ingredients.

“We have a lot of people here who are also on government-issued food stamps because they are on a low income and have a low education, so they don’t know how to read ingredients and what calories mean.



“They then get hooked on the sugar and additives, so it’s a domino effect.

“There’s a link between the two socio-economically.”

One 5ft 8in local, who weighs at least 43st, lives his life entirely in his bed because of his extreme weight.

The man, who has asked for his identity to be concealed, says he used to have substance abuse issues. After quitting drugs, he replaced his fix with food.

He explains: “I would eat three McChicken burgers, a Big Mac combo, cookies, 20-piece nuggets with the sauce, large fries, and, after that, I would eat three more meals.



“I would get full, but my mind would tell me I was still hungry.

“I gained 200lbs (14st 4lbs) in nine months, and now I can’t even fit through my door.”



Even a visit to a petrol station in McAllen sees locals filling up more than their cars.

The restaurants on the forecourt sell some of the most calorific meals in the city, with a simple dish of chicken and rice coming in at just under 2,000 calories.

While more than 40 per cent of US adults are obese, and nearly three in four are considered overweight or obese, the US government is focusing on improving healthy food access, increasing taxes on sugary drinks and providing FDA-approved medication.

But I am told fat jabs like Ozempic and Mounjaro, which have surged in the US, with 12 per cent of adults on them, are not considered in McAllen.

BIG LOSERS HERE are three US cities that tackled their obesity crisis in interesting ways: OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA IN one of the nation’s most obese cities, mayor Mick Cornett led a campaign in 2008 for locals to lose a collective one million pounds in weight, bringing in initiatives to build more pavements and parks plus better public transport. They met the goal by 2012. MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA CONSISTENTLY ranked as one of the healthiest cities in America, Minneapolis curbs obesity by banning new restaurant drive-thrus and strives to make the city more walkable. HUNTINGTON, WEST VIRGINIA DUBBED “America’s fattest city” in 2008, it has reduced its obesity rate from 44 per cent to roughly 32 per cent as of 2019. While still above the national average, the city achieved this through community-wide health initiatives and lifestyle changes.

This is due to a mix of locals not being able to afford them — more than 20 per cent of residents live in poverty, and one in four households is on benefits — as well as citizens ­simply feeling that “fat is the norm”.



It is a chilling glimpse into how ­serious the UK’s obesity crisis could become.

Almost 30 per cent of adults in England are living with obesity, with 66 per cent classified as overweight or obese, creating a major public health crisis.

McAllen bartender Sam, who weighs 17st, is trying to lose weight by ditching junk food, but says the real draw is the all-you-can-eat ­Chinese buffets.

He says: “We love it here. It’s only $12.99 (£9.50) for as much as you want. They even have signs to say, ‘Please do not eat in the buffet area’ because people are so addicted.”

Two teenage pals, Clarissa Garcia, 18, and Evely Soto, 19, say they are already on a dangerous trajectory.



They tell me: “We’ve tried to lose weight, but it’s so hard. It’s harder here than anywhere else.”

News.title: School mobile phone ban to be enforced by law in major new step
News.content:
School mobile phone ban to be enforced by law in major new step

Headteachers will have to ban pupils from using mobile phones during school hours under the new amendment planned by the government - the move will bring existing guidance into law

View Image School mobile phone bans will be made a legal requirement under new plans announced by the government (file photo) (Image: Getty Images)

Children will be banned from using mobile phones at school by law under new plans unveiled by the government.

‌



Number 10 will seek to make phone bans in schools statutory by introducing an amendment in the House of Lords to the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill.

‌



Currently, Department for Education (DfE) advises headteachers to stop pupils from using the devices on school grounds - but they are free to ignore this guidance if they wish.

‌



The new amendment will make existing guidance on mobile phone bans in schools statutory.

Which social media sites could face UK ban - as PM meets Facebook and Google READ MORE :

Parents 'disgusted' by Liverpool school toilet ban during lessons READ MORE :

A spokesperson for the DfE said: "We have been consistently clear that mobile phones have no place in schools, and the majority already prohibit them. "This amendment makes existing guidance statutory, giving legal force to what schools are already doing in practice. "It builds on the steps we've already taken to strengthen enforcement, with Ofsted considering schools' mobile phone policies as part of inspection from this month. "We will always put children's interests first, including through this Bill - which is widely recognised as the biggest piece of child safeguarding legislation in decades, with critical measures like laws to crack down on profiteering in children's social care and a new unique identifier to stop children falling through the cracks."

‌



It comes after a recent survey of more than 15,000 schools found that the vast majority already have policies in place restricting the use of phones.

In the national study, ordered by children’s commissioner for England Rachel de Souza, 99.8% of primary schools and 90% of secondary schools reported having some form of ban.

Daniel Kebede, general secretary of the National Education Union (NEU), said in response to the findings: "My personal view is I would support a statutory ban on mobile phones in schools. I think it would alleviate pressure on school leaders and teachers but also parents.

Article continues below

“I think there is a much-needed conversation to be had in this country about mobile phone use, online harm and the damaging impact that it has on our young people.

“The average 12-year-old has access to the most hardcore pornography on their mobile phone, and that is incredibly damaging to the wellbeing of young boys and their perceptions of women and girls, sex and relationships.”

News.title: 10 major points as Keir Starmer says Peter Mandelson vetting scandal 'beggars belief'
News.content:
10 major points as Keir Starmer says Peter Mandelson vetting scandal 'beggars belief'

Keir Starmer said he is 'frankly staggered' he was not told Peter Mandelson had failed security vetting - here are the key points from his more than two-hour long Commons statement

View 6 Images Keir Starmer said it 'beggars belief' he was not told Peter Mandelson had failed vetting (Image: House of Commons/UK Parliament/PA Wire)

Keir Starmer has told MPs he is “frankly staggered” that he was not told Peter Mandelson hadn't passed security vetting.

‌



In a statement lasting more than two hours in the Commons, the PM said the sequence of events leading to this "beggars belief" as he expressed his anger and frustration at officials in the Foreign Office for not keeping him informed.

‌



The PM said he would not have proceeded with the appointment of Lord Mandelson if he had known UK Security Vetting (UKSV), the agency responsible for conducting assessments, had declined to approve the peer.

‌



He told the chamber he has stripped the Foreign Office of its powers to overrule vetting decisions and has ordered an extensive review into how security vetting decisions are made.

The Mirror looks back at some of the key points from the statement.

Keir Starmer watch LIVE: PM lashes out in heated Mandelson grilling as furious MP kicked out READ MORE :

View 6 Images It emerged last week that Peter Mandelson failed security vetting (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



1. Beggars belief

Keir Starmer told MPs there was “deliberate decision” taken on “repeated occasions” not to tell him about Lord Peter Mandelson’s failure to pass security vetting. And he said the process that led to senior politicians and officials not being told about the security vetting status of Lord Mandelson “beggars belief”.

He told MPs: “I know many members across the House will find these facts to be incredible, and to that I can only say that they are right. It beggars belief that throughout the whole timeline of events, officials in the Foreign Office saw fit to withhold this information from the most senior ministers in our system of government. “That is not how the vast majority of people in this country expects politics, government or accountability to work, and I do not think it’s how most public servants think it should work.”

2. Review into security vetting

Keir Starmer said he was “frankly staggered” about not being told about UK Security Vetting (UKSV) recommending that Lord Peter Mandelson not be given developed vetting clearance. The Prime Minister said he has stripped the Foreign Office of its powers to overrule vetting decisions and has appointed Sir Adrian Fulford to lead a review into how security vetting decisions are made.

‌



Mr Starmer said: “I do not accept that I could not have been told about UKSV’s denial of security vetting before Peter Mandelson took up his post in January 2025. I do not accept that the then-cabinet secretary could not have been told in September 2025 when he carried out his review into the process.

“I do not accept that the Foreign Secretary could not have been told when making statements to the select committee, again in 2025. But on top of that the fact that I was not told even when I ordered a review of the UKSV process, is frankly staggering, and I can tell the House that I’ve now updated the terms of reference for the review into security vetting to make sure it covers the means by which all decisions are made in relation to national security vetting.”

View 6 Images Keir Starmer took questions from MPs for more than two hours (Image: PRU/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



3. Heat from Labour MPs

Keir Starmer faced heat from left-wing MPs in the chamber during the statement - including Labour figures.

Veteran MP Diane Abbott, who does not currently have the Labour whip and is the longest-serving female MP, criticised Mr Starmer for talking at length about "process and procedure". She continued: "Ordinary people don't really care about process and procedure. They want transparency and they want to know that they can have confidence in the words of elected politicians... It's one thing to say, as he insists on saying, nobody told me, nobody told me anything, nobody told me. The question is, why didn't the Prime Minister ask?"

Left-wing Labour MP John McDonnell said many Labour MPs are "bewildered" that Lord Mandelson was appointed in the first place. He hit out at the Prime Minister’s former official Morgan McSweeney, who had a close relationship with Lord Mandelson. “What Mandelson wants, Mandelson gets,” Mr McDonnell said. He was heckled by members of the Cabinet as he spoke.

‌



Other Labour backbenchers queried why politicians were not told about Lord Mandelson’s vetting. Alistair Strathern (Hitchin) said: “Many of my constituents are rightly concerned to learn that not a single democratically elected official in Government was informed.” His comments were echoed by his colleague Rachel Blake.

View 6 Images Veteran MP Diane Abbott said the public wants 'confidence in the words of elected politicians' (Image: Vuk Valcic/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

4. Starmer faces demands to quit

The PM faced a blistering attack from Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey, who called on him to quit.

‌



He told MPs “the only decent thing” for Mr Starmer to do “is to take responsibility”. And in a brutal insult, he compared Mr Starmer to Boris Johnson, saying: “Back in 2022, the Prime Minister rightly accused Boris Johnson of expecting others to take the blame while he clung on. That was not acceptable then, and it’s not acceptable now.”

He continued: "After the years of chaos under the Conservatives, we needed a government focused on the interests of the people, the cost of living crisis, the health and care crisis, our national security. We needed a government honesty, integrity and accountability. So will the Prime Minister finally accept that the only way he can help to deliver that is to resign?"

Mr Starmer responded he was told “the process was as it should have been” when the Bloomberg emails came to light, adding: “When I asked the former cabinet secretary to review the process after September 25, he specifically addressed whether the process had been followed by referencing the Simon Case letter, and assured me that the process was the right process to have followed.”

‌



5. Suggestion Mandelson leaked own appointment

The chair of the Foreign Affairs Select Committee has suggested that Mandelson could have leaked his appointment to "bounce" the Government.

Dame Emily Thornberry said: "A month before Mandelson's appointment was announced, the then-Cabinet Secretary advised that the necessary security clearance should be acquired before confirming a political appointment.

"That doesn't seem to have been the usual practice. I'm glad that it's changed because it was clearly abused, because what happened was that somebody, probably Peter Mandelson himself, leaked to the press his appointment as US ambassador, effectively bouncing the government into confirming it."

‌



6. Apology to Epstein victims

Mr Starmer has long faced pressure for his decision to appoint Peter Mandelson as Britain's Ambassador to the US given the Labour grandee's long reported links to Jeffrey Epstein.

Lord Mandelson was sacked from the role in September after new information came to light about the pair's relationship in the Epstein files released by the US government.

During the debate, multiple MPs told the PM he shouldn't have appointed Lord Mandelson in the first place due to his Epstein links. Mr Starmer told MPs today: “At the heart of this, there is also a judgment I made that was wrong. I should not have appointed Peter Mandelson.

‌



“I take responsibility for that decision, and I apologise again to the victims of the paedophile Jeffrey Epstein, who were clearly failed by my decision.”

View 6 Images Lord Mandelson was sacked as Britain's Ambassador to the US after new information came to light about his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

7. Normal to appoint before security vetting

Keir Starmer has reiterated that it was “usual” for security vetting to take place following an appointment. In a statement to the Commons, the Prime Minister said: “I want to make clear to the House that for a direct ministerial appointment, it was usual for security vetting to happen after the appointment, but before starting in post, that was the process in place at the time. This was confirmed by the former cabinet secretary, Sir Chris Wormald at the Foreign Affairs Select Committee on the 3rd of November 2025, when he gave evidence. “Sir Chris made clear, I’m quoting him now, ‘when we are making appointments from outside the Civil Service, the normal thing is for security clearance to happen after appointment, but before the person signs a contract and takes up post’.” He continued: “After I sacked Peter Mandelson I changed that process so that now an appointment cannot be announced until after security vetting is passed.”

‌



8. PM rejects Olly Robbins explanation

Mr Starmer has said he did not accept Sir Olly Robbin's explanation - which led to his sacking last week. The PM said former Foreign Office chief Sir Olly did not tell him the recommendation of United Kingdom Security Vetting (UKSV) because he did not believe he was allowed to.

The PM told MPs: "He (Sir Olly) should have provided this information to me, and he could have provided it to me. He's giving evidence tomorrow, but I can say to the House that, when I spoke to him on Thursday, his view to me was that he couldn't provide this information to me, because he wasn't allowed to provide information to me.

"I don't want to put words in his mouth, because it's very important he gives his own evidence."

‌



The Prime Minister added: "What he (Sir Olly) said to me was, essentially, that he took the view that this process did not allow him to disclose to me the recommendation of UKSV. No doubt he'll be asked further questions about that. That is the reason that he gave to me." Mr Starmer said he "did not accept his explanation".

9. PM unable to say if Mandelson-style appointments made

Keir Starmer was unable to say whether there are any other Mandelson-style political appointments to the Foreign Office.

Lib Dem MP Edward Morello pressed him to find out if it was a one-off. He asked: "This entire sorry episode is the direct result of his decision to make a direct appointment to one of the most senior roles in the FCDO of somebody who was wholly inappropriate for the role.

‌



"So can the Prime Minister at least confirm to the House that this was a singular error of judgment, and that his No10 operation has not proposed political appointee for any other senior role in the FCDO?"

Mr Starmer responded: "There are very many appointments... and I will just check that for him."

View 6 Images Lee Anderson was kicked out of the Commons after accusing Keir Starmer of lying (Image: PRU/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



10. Two MPs kicked out after accusing PM of lying

Lee Anderson and Zarah Sultana were kicked out of the Commons after accusing Keir Starmer of lying during the debate.

Reform UK MP Mr Anderson told Mr Starmer: "The problem the Prime Minister's got is no one believes him. The public don't believe him, the MPs on this side of the House don't believe him, his own gullible backbenchers don't believe him. So does the Prime Minister agree with me? He's been lying."

Later, Your Party MP Zarah Sultana was also ordered out of the chamber after calling Mr Starmer a liar. A furious Ms Sultana, who used to sit on the Labour benches, said: "He (Mr Starmer) is gaslighting the nation. So let's call this out for what it is. The Prime Minister is a barefaced liar."

Article continues below

Sir Lindsay Hoyle told the MPs to leave the chambers on each of the occasions.

On social media, Labour MP Jacob Collier said: "Two MPs kicked out of the Chamber for unparliamentary behaviour, purely so they can put a clip on social media for their supporters. Appalling conduct."

News.title: West Mercia Police officer stabbed in neck while on duty and rushed to hospital
News.content:
West Mercia Police officer stabbed in neck while on duty and rushed to hospital

A 25-year-old suspect is being held in custody after officers were called to reports of a man acting suspiciously in Clifton, near Kempsey, Worcestershire

View Image A West Mercia Police officer has been stabbed in the neck (stock image) (Image: Emma Trimble / SWNS)

A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a female police officer was stabbed in the neck, West Mercia Police said.

‌



The force said the 25-year-old suspect is being held in custody after officers were called to reports of a man acting suspiciously in Clifton, near Kempsey, Worcestershire, at around 7.30pm on Sunday.

‌



The police officer was attacked while conducting searches of the area. Police said she was treated for her injuries and has been discharged from hospital.

‌



Chief Superintendent Edd Williams said: “This is a truly shocking incident, and our thoughts are with the officer who was injured.

“Police officers are dedicated to protecting people, and to be attacked while doing their job is abhorrent.

Article continues below

“I’m pleased that the officer has now been discharged from hospital, although the outcome could easily have been very different.

“The man arrested remains in custody and officers will remain in the area today as inquiries continue.”

News.title: M62 traffic live: Yorkshire motorway closed after pile-up as vehicle in flames
News.content:
There are currently delays of around 30 minutes with three miles of congestion as multiple lanes on the M62 in West Yorkshire have closed following a multi-vehicle collision

Drivers are facing long queues on the M62 this evening as a multi-vehicle collision has forced multiple lanes to close.

There are currently delays of around 30 minutes with three miles of congestion as the eastbound carriageway in West Yorkshire has been closed between J29 and J30. The crash happened between junction 29 for the M1 at Lofthouse and junction 30 at Rothwell at around 4:15pm.

Three out of four lanes on the westbound side of the carriageway have also closed.

News.title: Tiny 7 foot home for sale for huge price - it packs in so much
News.content:
Tiny 7 foot home for sale for huge price - it packs in so much

Despite being just 7ft wide, the property packs in more than many much larger homes

View 4 Images (Image: Jam Press/Unique Property Company)

A tiny home that is reportedly London's second narrowest has hit the market. And it's up for sale for an eye-watering price despite its size.

‌



The residence has been listed for an eye-popping £1.2 million. Measuring a mere seven feet across, the compact dwelling stands out conspicuously on Peel Street in Kensington.

‌



View 4 Images There is so much packed inside this home (Image: Jam Press/Unique Property Company)

‌



Yet appearances can be misleading – and within, the homeowners have ingeniously fitted two bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen diner and reception room, plus its own private terrace. Despite its modest proportions, it demonstrates that location truly matters – with its desirable Notting Hill Gate setting adding considerable worth.

Intelligently arranged across three storeys, the house dates back to 1930 and underwent renovation in the 1950s. The present occupant, who has owned the property for a decade, has meticulously planned the layout to maximise every available inch.

‌



View 4 Images A bedroom in the house (Image: Jam Press/Unique Property Company)

The entrance leads into the "Tardis-like" open plan kitchen and dining area, which are remarkably roomy, allowing space for entertaining – provided your visitors don't object to rather intimate surroundings. The ground floor also features a shower room and WC, along with one of the two bedrooms, according to creatorzine.com.

Ascending the stairs reveals a first-floor reception room, barely sufficient for a sofa and armchair, though largely taken up by the fireplace. However, any sense of confinement is relieved – the space extends onto a decked rear terrace with sufficient room for outdoor dining. On the second floor, you'll discover a top floor suite featuring stylish front-facing slash windows alongside an en suite bathroom.

Article continues below

View 4 Images They have made the most of the space (Image: Jam Press/Unique Property Company)

Should you fancy venturing beyond the property, both Kensington Gardens and Holland Park are within easy walking distance – not to mention the vibrant city centre beyond. The property is presently available through Unique Property Company, with an asking price of £1,195,000.

News.title: Wolverhampton dog attack victim's family pay heartbreaking tribute to 'everyone's friend'
News.content:
Wolverhampton dog attack victim's family pay heartbreaking tribute to 'everyone's friend'

Lila Hall, also known as Carol, died following an incident with two dogs at a house in Willis Pearson Avenue, Wolverhampton

View Image Dog attack victim Carol Hall (Image: facebook)

The family of a woman who was killed in a dog attack have remembered her as a "fun-loving" and "hilarious" woman who was "everyone's friend".

‌



Lila Hall - also known as Carol - died following an incident with two dogs at a house in Willis Pearson Avenue, Wolverhampton, last week.

This is a breaking news story.

News.title: Winston-Salem mass shooting horror as two dead after 'planned fight' near schools
News.content:
Winston-Salem mass shooting horror as two dead after 'planned fight' near schools

Several young people are said to have been involved in a brawl which escalated into a mass shooting and saw two people killed in the North Carolina town of Winston-Salem

View 3 Images Police are responding to a shooting in Winston-Salem (Image: WFMY News 2 /Youtube)

Police have swarmed a park in a north Carolina town after a "planned fight" escalated into a mass shooting, leaving two people dead.

‌



Several young people are said to have been involved in the brawl at Leinbach Park in Winston-Salem, which has reportedly left multiple people injured. The North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation (NC SBI) said the incident, which happened at around 9:52am local time, was a "mass shooting" and that two people have died as a result.

‌



Winston-Salem police are yet to confirm the total number of victims, but the NC SBI said "several people" had been shot.

‌



"The NC SBI is currently responding to a shooting on Robinhood Road near Jefferson Middle School," it said in a post on Facebook.

View 3 Images The shooting happened at Leinbach Park in Winston-Salem (Image: WFMY News 2 /Youtube)

"The shooting is NOT at the school but in Leinbach Park. The school is now operating regularly and is open. Several people have been shot, with 2 deceased. People should avoid the area for now."

‌



Investigators have asked members of the public to avoid the use of personal drones as this may interfere with ongoing emergency operations. Police drones are being used to search for "involved individuals".

Officers said several people - both victims and suspects - have been identified and located, but due to the number of individuals involved, efforts are ongoing to account for everyone. "At this time, some of those involved in the incident are juveniles," the Winston-Salem Police Department said.

View 3 Images Members of the public have been asked to report any suspicious activity (Image: WFMY News 2 /Youtube)

‌



"Initial investigations suggest a planned fight involving several young individuals escalated at a park, leading to multiple people shooting at each other. There are multiple victims. Suspects remain outstanding.

"At this time, this remains an active and ongoing investigation following a shooting incident that began earlier this morning near Leinbach Park at Sally Kirk Rd."

"A large police presence continues in the area as officers actively investigate."

Article continues below

Police say nearby schools are currently operating on a normal schedule but have urged community members to avoid the area to allow emergency responders to operate safely. Authorities have also the public to remain alert and report "any suspicious activity".

News.title: Britain's first vending machine for chips launched - but opinion is divided
News.content:
Britain's first vending machine for chips launched - but opinion is divided

A first-of-its-kind vending machine serves up chips at the touch of a button and even offers the option of salt or ketchup, with the company behind it promising to roll them out across the country

View 3 Images A vending machine in Wrexham serves up piping hot chips - and is set to be followed by others across the country

Britain's first vending machine for chips has been unveiled - and you can get your dinner by just tapping a screen. Captain Chip say their £2.99 self-serve chip vending machine in Wrexham city centre will followed by others in London, with the treat served up in a box. But getting your chips in the same way as a bar of chocolate or crisps has split shoppers - with some labelling the new contraption "ridiculous." It says in 160 seconds, customers can walk away with a pot of piping hot chips in hand - even having the option of getting them salted or with ketchup.

‌



Man fights for life after horror attack in Stockbridge Village chip shop READ MORE :

One word to look for when ordering fish and chips after 'avoid' warning READ MORE :

View 3 Images Diners even have the option of salt or ketchup

‌



Bosses at Captain Chip say that the response to the machine has so far been 'brilliant'. A spokesperson added: "Wrexham felt like the right place to launch this concept.

‌



"Eagles Meadow shopping centre is a hub for the community, and Captain Chip is designed to slot into moments where people want something hot, quick and satisfying without queuing or committing to a full sit-down meal."

The Captain Chip installation in Wrexham marks one of the first public locations for the concept, placing the North Wales city at the forefront of a growing trend in automated food experiences that combine convenience with quality. The machine is fully self-contained and operates without the need for permanent staffing.

‌



View 3 Images The innovation has split opinion, with some diners saying they prefer to buy their chips the 'old fashioned' way

One shopper said the chips "seem expensive when you can get a cone in Jones Chippy for under £2", while another added: "We got some a few weeks ago and they weren't the best. Who thought of this when trade is already dying and these proper chippies and food places are struggling to make profit already?" Others saw the funnier side - with an imaginative shopper joking: "I feel sorry for the person all day sat inside it peeling spuds!"

It comes as rising energy bills and surging fish costs have sent the cost of Britain's favourite dish soaring in recent years, forcing many chip shops to reluctantly up their prices.

The government is set to make mobile phone bans in schools statutory, introducing an amendment to the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill in the House of Lords.

A Department for Education (DfE) spokesperson said the change will formalise existing guidance on phone restrictions in educational settings.

The spokesperson said: “We have been consistently clear that mobile phones have no place in schools, and the majority already prohibit them.

“This amendment makes existing guidance statutory, giving legal force to what schools are already doing in practice.

“It builds on the steps we’ve already taken to strengthen enforcement, with Ofsted considering schools’ mobile phone policies as part of inspection from this month.

“We will always put children’s interests first, including through this bill – which is widely recognised as the biggest piece of child safeguarding legislation in decades, with critical measures like laws to crack down on profiteering in children’s social care and a new unique identifier to stop children falling through the cracks.”

open image in gallery The education secretary has previously written to headteachers in England to stress that schools should be phone-free throughout the entire school day ( Jane Barlow/PA )

Peers will vote in the Lords on Monday evening on a Conservative amendment to the bill on mobile phones.

Bridget Phillipson, the education secretary, has previously written to headteachers in England to stress that schools should be phone-free throughout the entire school day. However, guidance to schools on mobile phones has been non-statutory.

The teaching union NASUWT has previously announced its support for a statutory school phone ban.

A government source said: “The repeated attempts by the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats to kill off some of the most far-reaching child protection legislation is an utterly abhorrent, and a [sic] dismal failure of some of the most vulnerable children in our country.

“After more than a decade where children’s social care and the system of child safeguarding was left to rot by these parties in office, and that saw horrific child abuse cases such as those of Arthur Labinjo Hughes, Star Hobson and Sara Sharif, this government moved quickly to fix what was broken – only to be thwarted at every turn by opposition parties.

“The blocking of measures in this legislation, which includes direct manifesto commitments, such as the introduction of free breakfast clubs and limits to branded school uniform, saving families hundreds of pounds, by unelected Conservative and Liberal Democrat peers, is a complete affront to democracy.”

A popular gas station and convenience store chain wants customers to fly instead of drive.

Wawa plans to swap drive-thrus with “Fly Thru” mobile pickup windows at certain new store openings in the Midwest, according to multiple reports, where the company has already added Fly Thru to three existing stores. The convenience store, which has drawn praise for its made-to-order subs, sandwiches and drinks, is introducing the mobile windows six years after opening its first drive-thru locations in 2020

The mobile pickup windows will allow customers to order food and pick it up within 30 seconds without leaving their cars, Delaware-based Delco Today reported.

Wawa President Brian Schaller said during a company event this past week that he believes mobile pickup windows are “where the future is.”

The Independent requested information about Fly Thru from Wawa, including how many stores will feature the mobile ordering windows and the company’s plans to expand them beyond Midwest states, but had not received a response as of publication.

open image in gallery Wawa’s latest move to improve operations is one that its president says is “where the future is” ( Getty Images )

Wawa joins several other companies that invested in drive-thrus and mobile ordering pickup during the pandemic, as customers practiced social distancing measures that typically included keeping six feet between people.

Mobile pickup, in particular, proved a valuable asset for restaurants and retail stores during the pandemic. Their importance was immense, with many businesses seeing double-digit growth in their e-commerce departments.

Drive-thrus were also a focal point of several big companies’ investments.

“Drive-thrus proved to be a lifeline for fast-food chains such as McDonald’s and Wendy’s, which reported more moderate same-store sales declines as lockdowns went into effect and revenue that bounced back more quickly,” CNBC reported in August 2020.

The moves that Wawa has made over the past few years to improve customer experience seem to be working. It’s expanded its U.S. footprint from six states in 2023 to at least a dozen in 2026.

Since 2020, the company has also introduced an expanded menu that includes burgers and pizzas. Its bigger menu has helped Wawa pull market share from well-known fast-food and fast casual competitors, CNBC reported in October 2025. Customers who shop at both Wawa and Burger King, Wendy’s or Starbucks shop at Wawa more frequently than the others since 2023, CNBC found.

open image in gallery Wawa’s reputation as a customer-focused convenience store has helped it stay competitive with other convenience stores such as Buc-ee’s, Sheetz and Kwik Trip ( Getty/Wiki Commons )

On the convenience store side, Wawa’s customer base grew from August 2023 to August 2025, CNBC reported, while competitors 7-11, Circle K and Sheetz lost customers during that same period.

Not only has Wawa made strides against competitors in several different industries, but it’s won the hearts of American consumers, too. The company was named the country’s favorite convenience store in 2024, according to the results of the American Customer Satisfaction Index Convenience Store Study 2024.

News.content:

As he set out his defence to the House of Commons, Sir Keir Starmer was asked multiple times by MPs, including the Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch, about The Independent’s front page story on 12 September last year that Peter Mandelson had failed security vetting.

More damaging still are the WhatsApp messages sent by this publication to the then director of communications in Downing Street, Tim Allan, raising the issue on 11 September.

This has been described by a number of civil servants and senior politicians as the “smoking gun” in the entire scandal, because it is at odds with the prime minister’s own assessment.

Sir Keir claimed that he, his ministers and Downing Street only found out about the security vetting failure last week. But doubt has been cast on this claim because The Independent informed Downing Street’s most senior communications official months before.

Added to that it raises serious questions about what the prime minister was told in September by his then director of communications.

open image in gallery Prime minister Sir Keir Starmer is under fire again over his decision to appoint Lord Mandelson ( PA Wire )

In normal circumstances these issues are raised through the system and lead to investigations about the truth. Most crucially they are raised with the prime minister and should have been a red flag.

But it seems that nothing happened and the warnings were ignored.

This is no small thing. Lord Mandelson spent months as the UK’s ambassador to Washington.

He was the most important UK diplomat in the United States, at a time when Britain was grappling with a difficult president in the White House.

And, as ambassador, he would have been party to a huge amount of information, some of it designed only for those who would have passed the highest level of security vetting.

When the prime minister sacked him last September, he accused Mandelson of lying to his officials during that process and said he had fired him when the full extent of his relationship with the paedophile financier Jeffrey Epstein emerged.

And then, crucially, in February, Sir Keir told journalists: “Security vetting, carried out independently by the security services, which is an intensive exercise that gave him clearance for the role. You have to go through that before you take up the post. Clearly both the due diligence and the security vetting need to be looked at again.”

But this took place months after The Independent informed No 10 of the failure.

open image in gallery Lord Mandelson (right) pictured with Jeffrey Epstein (centre) and Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor (left), in a photograph released as part of the Epstein files. ( US Department of Justice )

On Monday the PM insisted that he should have been told last year that his former man in Washington had failed security clearance. But, of course, Downing Street was told. By The Independent.

Last week Sir Keir said he was “furious” when he found out and that it was unacceptable he was not told.

Within hours he had fired the most senior civil servant in the Foreign Office Olly Robbins. That, Sir Keir has been very clear, was because Mr Robbins was aware of the recommendation not to give Mandelson security clearance and did not inform the prime minister.

But Sir Keir still faces a key question, one which was summed up by the mother of the House, the long-time Labour MP Diane Abbott who is currently suspended from the party and sits as an independent MP.

She cornered him in the Commons to ask him: “It’s one thing to say, as (Starmer) insists on saying nobody told me, nobody told me anything, nobody told me. The question is, why didn’t the prime minister ask?”
